title: Grade 4 CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — 3.1 The Annunciation

pages.lesson:
PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

The annunciation is the announcement of the birth of Jesus Christ. In Luke 1:26-37 the angel Gabriel tells Mary that she will give birth to Jesus. In this sub-strand you will narrate that event, see why His birth is unique, recite Luke 1:37, and learn from Mary's holy life.

## Strand 3.0: The Life of Jesus Christ
Sub-strand 3.1: The Annunciation
Suggested lessons: 3

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) narrate the annunciation of the Birth of Jesus Christ
b) acknowledge the uniqueness of the birth of Jesus Christ
c) recite Luke 1:37 and trust in God’s power
d) emulate Mary the mother of Jesus and lead a holy life

## Key inquiry questions
1. Why is the birth of Jesus Christ unique?

## Core competencies
• Imagination and Creativity: the skill of coming up with new ideas is exhibited as learners role-play the annunciation of the birth of Jesus Christ.

## Values
• Unity: learners work in pairs and groups to perform different tasks.

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• Human Sexuality- Abstinence: learners emulate Mary the mother of Jesus Christ by leading holy lives and abstaining from sex before marriage.

## Links to other learning areas
• Creative Arts: creative skills are reinforced as learners sing and role play.
• English: reading skills are applied as learners read the Holy Bible.

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 Christian Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 3.0 The Life of Jesus Christ, Sub-strand 3.1 The Annunciation
• Luke 1:26-37

PAGE 2: Lesson 1: The angel's message to Mary

LESSON 1: THE ANGEL'S MESSAGE TO MARY
=====================================

## What you will learn
• Narrate the annunciation from Luke 1:26-37 in order.
• Name the people in the account and the message about Jesus.

Curriculum outcomes: a) narrate the annunciation of the Birth of Jesus Christ

## Introduction
Good news is sometimes brought by a messenger. God sent the angel Gabriel to a young woman in Nazareth with the news that she would be the mother of Jesus.

## Notes
Annunciation means an announcement. This announcement is the birth of Jesus Christ. Read Luke 1:26-37 in turns and narrate only what those verses say.

### The visit
In the sixth month of Elizabeth's pregnancy, God sent the angel Gabriel to Nazareth, a town in Galilee. He went to a virgin named Mary. She was pledged to be married to Joseph, a descendant of David. The angel said, "Greetings, you who are highly favoured! The Lord is with you."

Mary was greatly troubled and wondered what kind of greeting this was. The angel told her not to be afraid. She had found favour with God. She would conceive and give birth to a son, and she must name Him Jesus.

### Who the child would be
The angel said Jesus would be great and would be called the Son of the Most High. The Lord God would give Him the throne of His father David. He would reign over Jacob's descendants forever. His kingdom would never end.

### Mary's question
Mary asked how this could be, since she was a virgin. The angel answered that the Holy Spirit would come upon her and the power of the Most High would overshadow her. The holy one to be born would be called the Son of God. The angel also said that Elizabeth, Mary's relative, was going to have a child in her old age, and that she was already in her sixth month. Luke 1:37 says that no word from God will ever fail. With God, nothing is impossible.

When you narrate, keep this order: Gabriel sent to Mary in Nazareth; the greeting; her trouble; the name Jesus; the throne of David and the kingdom that never ends; her question; the Holy Spirit; Elizabeth; the promise that God's word does not fail.

## Key words
• annunciation — the announcement of the birth of Jesus Christ
• virgin — a person who has not had sexual relations; Luke 1:27 describes Mary in this way
• angel Gabriel — the angel God sent to Mary
• favour — God's special kindness

## Activity: Read and role-play the annunciation
You will need: Bible, Space to act
1. In turns, read Luke 1:26-37.
2. Role-play the annunciation: Gabriel, Mary, and a narrator.
3. If a video clip of the annunciation is available, watch it and say which parts match the reading.
4. In groups, retell the announcement in the correct order.

## Practice
1. Who brought the announcement to Mary, and where did she live?
2. What name was Mary to give the child, and whose throne would He receive?
3. How did the angel say Mary would conceive, since she was a virgin?

## Summary
• Gabriel announced to Mary in Nazareth that she would give birth to Jesus.
• Jesus would be the Son of the Most High, and His kingdom would never end.
• Mary was a virgin. The child would be conceived by the Holy Spirit.

### Answers to practice
1. The angel Gabriel came to Mary in Nazareth in Galilee.
2. She was to name Him Jesus. God would give Him the throne of His father David.
3. The Holy Spirit would come upon her, and the power of the Most High would overshadow her.

PAGE 3: Lesson 2: A unique birth and Luke 1:37

LESSON 2: A UNIQUE BIRTH AND LUKE 1:37
======================================

## What you will learn
• Explain why the birth of Jesus Christ is unique.
• Recite Luke 1:37 and say what it means to trust God's power.

Curriculum outcomes: b) acknowledge the uniqueness of the birth of Jesus Christ; c) recite Luke 1:37 and trust in God’s power

## Introduction
Many children are born into families. The birth announced to Mary is different from every other birth. Luke 1:37 tells us why such a thing could be promised.

## Notes
Unique means one of a kind. The birth of Jesus is unique for reasons that Luke 1:26-37 itself gives.

### Why this birth is unique
- Mary was a virgin. She said so to the angel.
- The child would be conceived by the Holy Spirit, not in the ordinary way.
- He would be called the Son of the Most High and the Son of God.
- He would sit on David's throne and reign forever. His kingdom would never end.
- The announcement came from God through the angel Gabriel, not from a human plan.

No other baby in the passage is described in this way. Elizabeth's child was a wonderful gift in her old age, and the angel used that gift as a sign. Jesus' birth is still different, because He is the Son of God.

### Luke 1:37
The verse teaches that nothing is impossible with God. His word does not fail. Mary could trust the promise because of who God is, not because she could see how a virgin would bear a child.

Recite the verse: "For there is nothing that God cannot do." Meditate on it. Sit quietly and think of one thing that seems too hard for you. Then remember that God's power is greater than that hard thing. Trust means depending on Him.

### Trust in daily life
You trust God's power when you pray about a sick relative, a fear, or a problem you cannot fix. You also work and obey. Trust is not laziness. It is refusing to believe that God is too weak to keep His word. The annunciation happened because God's word does not fail.

## Key words
• unique — one of a kind
• trust — to depend on God's power and His word
• impossible — something people cannot do; Luke 1:37 says it is not impossible for God

## Activity: Recite and meditate on Luke 1:37
You will need: Bible, Flash cards
1. Write Luke 1:37 on a flash card.
2. Recite it together, then meditate quietly on God's power.
3. In groups, list the facts that make the birth of Jesus unique.
4. Sing a song about the annunciation of the birth of Jesus Christ.

## Practice
1. Give two reasons why the birth of Jesus is unique.
2. What does Luke 1:37 teach?
3. How can a learner trust God's power?

## Summary
• Jesus' birth is unique because He was conceived by the Holy Spirit and is the Son of God.
• His kingdom will never end.
• Luke 1:37: nothing is impossible with God.

### Answers to practice
1. Any two: Mary was a virgin; He was conceived by the Holy Spirit; He is the Son of God; His kingdom will never end; the angel Gabriel announced Him.
2. Nothing is impossible with God. His word does not fail.
3. By praying, depending on His word, and remembering that God can do what people cannot do.

PAGE 4: Lesson 3: Learning from Mary's holy life

LESSON 3: LEARNING FROM MARY'S HOLY LIFE
========================================

## What you will learn
• Describe Mary's response as a holy example.
• Explain why sexual purity matters for young people.

Curriculum outcomes: d) emulate Mary the mother of Jesus and lead a holy life

## Introduction
Mary was highly favoured, and she was a virgin pledged to Joseph. Young Christians are asked to emulate her by leading a holy life.

## Notes
To emulate means to copy a good example. Mary is the mother of Jesus. Luke 1:26-37 shows her as a virgin who listened to God, asked an honest question, and heard that the Holy Spirit would do what people cannot do. She did not laugh at the angel. She did not treat God's message lightly.

### A holy life
Holy means set apart for God. Mary's life, as this passage presents it, was pure. She was pledged to be married, and she had kept herself a virgin. Christians honour that purity.

For a Grade 4 learner, leading a holy life means:

- Obeying God at home and at school.
- Keeping your body pure and saying no to sexual talk, pictures and touching that are wrong.
- Waiting until marriage for sex. That is abstinence, and it is part of holiness.
- Dressing neatly and respecting other people's bodies.
- Telling the truth and being kind, because holiness is more than one rule.
- Praying when you are tempted.

### Why sexual purity is important
God made our bodies as something precious. Sex is for marriage, not for childhood. Purity protects you from harm, from shame and from choices that are hard to undo. It also honours the God who sent Gabriel to a pure young woman. Say clearly in class why purity matters, using respectful words.

You emulate Mary when you trust God's word, as Luke 1:37 teaches, and when you keep your life clean for Him. Sing about the annunciation, and ask God for a holy heart.

## Key words
• emulate — to copy a good example
• holy life — a life set apart for God and kept pure
• purity — keeping yourself clean in body and behaviour, including saying no to sex before marriage

## Activity: Why purity is important
You will need: Bible
1. Read Luke 1:27 and 1:34 again and note that Mary was a virgin.
2. In groups, say why sexual purity is important, using respectful language.
3. Each learner says one way to emulate Mary this week.
4. Sing a song about the annunciation.

## Practice
1. What does emulate mean?
2. How is Mary an example of a holy life in Luke 1:26-37?
3. Give two ways a learner can lead a holy life.

## Summary
• Mary listened to God as a virgin highly favoured.
• Young Christians emulate her by living a holy and pure life.
• Sexual purity means keeping sex for marriage and saying no to what is wrong.

### Answers to practice
1. To copy a good example.
2. She was a virgin who listened to God's message and trusted what the angel said about the Holy Spirit.
3. Any two: obey God, keep the body pure, say no to wrong touching and bad pictures, wait until marriage for sex, pray when tempted, tell the truth.
pages.quiz:
REVISION QUIZ — 3.1 THE ANNUNCIATION
========================================

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. The annunciation is...
   A. the announcement of the birth of Jesus
   B. the death of John
   C. a parable about a coin
   D. the call of Abraham

2. God sent the angel Gabriel to Mary in...
   A. Bethlehem
   B. Nazareth
   C. Egypt
   D. Jericho

3. Mary was pledged to marry...
   A. Zechariah
   B. Joseph, a descendant of David
   C. Herod
   D. Pharaoh

4. The child was to be named...
   A. John
   B. Jesus
   C. Abraham
   D. David

5. Which fact shows that the birth of Jesus is unique?
   A. He would be conceived by the Holy Spirit and called the Son of God
   B. He was born in the ordinary way with no promise
   C. Mary refused to listen
   D. The angel said the kingdom would end quickly

6. His kingdom would...
   A. end after seven years
   B. never end
   C. belong to Balak
   D. stay only in Nazareth

7. Luke 1:37 teaches that...

8. Trusting God's power means...
   A. depending on His word
   B. laughing at His promises
   C. doing only what feels easy
   D. hiding from every problem without prayer

9. To emulate Mary means...
   A. to copy her holy example
   B. to ignore angels
   C. to leave Nazareth at once
   D. to refuse every question

10. Why is sexual purity important for a young Christian?
pages.answers:
ANSWERS — 3.1 THE ANNUNCIATION
========================================

1. A. the announcement of the birth of Jesus
   Annunciation means the announcement Gabriel brought to Mary.

2. B. Nazareth
   Luke 1:26 says Gabriel was sent to Nazareth in Galilee.

3. B. Joseph, a descendant of David
   Luke 1:27 names Joseph, a descendant of David.

4. B. Jesus
   Luke 1:31 says Mary must name Him Jesus.

5. A. He would be conceived by the Holy Spirit and called the Son of God
   Luke 1:34-35 gives the virgin birth by the Holy Spirit and the title Son of God.

6. B. never end
   Luke 1:33 says His kingdom will never end.

7. Nothing is impossible with God. His word does not fail.
   The verse is the reason Mary could trust the promise.

8. A. depending on His word
   Luke 1:37 is recited so learners trust God's power.

9. A. to copy her holy example
   Emulate means to follow a good example. Mary is the example of a holy life.

10. Because God wants a holy life, the body is precious, and sex is for marriage, not for childhood.
   The sub-strand links Mary's example with abstinence and holiness.
